entries.label: Infanterie à mousquet — Asie orientale
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit; regional/cultural variant.
Asset: ONE square full-canvas OPAQUE military-unit illustration for Victoria 3 mod 1776, preview only, no frame. Keep legible as a small icon.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and controls the composition, unit tier, weapon geometry, poses and painted finish. Image 2 is a VANILLA CULTURAL REFERENCE ONLY for faces and simple older dress; do NOT copy its other weapons, scene layout or irregular-unit status.
Request: create the Asie orientale (east_asian) counterpart to image 1, as a broad cultural-graphics family, not a claimed universal uniform or a named regiment.
Exactly three main musketeers. Preserve image 1's composition and actions: the prominent middle soldier is loading his long wood-stock flintlock musket with a vertical ramrod, the left soldier aims and the right soldier prepares his long musket. Keep each weapon, correct hand grips, individual natural faces, camera scale, light and soft oil-painted texture. This is the earlier infantry tier, an early-eighteenth-century visual evocation, clearly before later formal line infantry. Use a single modest brown cartridge-pouch belt, not bright white crossed straps. No rifles, percussion caps, nineteenth-century bayonet drill, armor, pikes or swords instead of muskets.
Clothing and people: Early-modern East Asian soldiers, with natural individually distinct East Asian faces. Dress in plain indigo, dull green and grey long front-fastened cotton tunics, loose trousers, cloth waist sashes and simple dark cloth caps or woven conical hats, based on image 2. Functional cloth garments, NOT European blue coats underneath Asian hats. No samurai plate armor, imperial dragon ornaments, feathered ceremonial helmet or nineteenth-century uniform.
Landscape: Hazy low green foothills and a few distant jagged mountains, without monumental buildings. Keep the original foreground layout, silhouettes and subdued oil-painted atmosphere. No huge geographic landmark, no nation flag or culture text. Small variations in garment wear, no identical cloned faces. Regional clothing must replace the European cut, not be layered on top of it.
Output: one finished cohesive painterly scene, full square with entirely opaque painted sky and ground. No sheet, comparison, captions, lettering, insignia, logos or watermark. No modern equipment.
